title: Model Slicing, Fallback Routing, and Graceful Degradation Guidelines
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview

This document defines a standard set of patterns, configuration knobs, and runbook procedures for model slicing, fallback routing, and graceful degradation in Redwood’s inference fleet. The goal is to provide predictable user experience during capacity constraints, degraded hardware, or model regressions while minimizing cost and blast radius.

When to apply these guidelines

- High load events where p95 latency or backend error rates exceed SLOs.
- Partial hardware outages (node-level GPU preemption, zone failures).
- Model quality regressions detected by automated evaluations or customer reports.
- Planned capacity maintenance and canary rollouts.

Principles

1) User-visible correctness first: avoid silent hallucinations. Prefer conservative fallbacks that preserve factuality even if they reduce responsiveness or richness.
2) Predictable, observable behavior: every routing decision must be logged with reason codes and tied to an SLI.
3) Minimal configuration surface for teams: use standardized profiles (see Profile table).
4) Fast automated recovery: default auto-fallbacks should be idempotent and reversible.

Key concepts

- Model slice: a model variant optimized for a particular cost/latency/quality tradeoff (e.g., m-1-quantized, m-1-shortseq, m-1-small).
- Fallback policy: ordered list of compatible slices to route to when the primary slice fails SLOs or is unavailable.
- Degradation mode: set of features temporarily disabled (e.g., streaming, multi-turn context, tool-calling) to reduce resource usage.
- Reason code: short tag attached to a routed request (examples: FALLBACK_LATENCY, FALLBACK_ERRORS, DEGRADE_SHORT_SEQ, CANARY_ROLLOUT).

Standard profiles (apply by model-service)

Profile | Target p95 (ms) | Typical slices (primary, fallback) | Default degradation
-------|------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------
interactive | 120 | full-fp32, quant-8, small-shortseq | disable streaming chunking
balanced | 250 | full-fp32, quant-8 | reduce KV cache TTL from 30s to 10s
throughput | 500 | quant-8, small-batched | enable batching 16, disable tool-calls

(Teams must set one profile per route in the route manifest.)

Routing and fallback rules (implementation guidance)

1) Every route has exactly one PrimarySlice and an ordered FallbackList. FallbackList entries must be semantically compatible (same tokenizer, same prompt template family).
2) The routing decision is evaluated per-request using these inputs: current p95 window (default 1m), node health flags, recent error ratio (5m), and per-customer tier policy. If any threshold is crossed, route to the first matching fallback slice.
3) Thresholds — default: p95_latency > profile.target_p95 * 1.25 OR error_rate_5m > 0.02 triggers FALLBACK_ERRORS.
4) If no compatible fallback exists, apply DegradationMode before returning 429/503: reduce max_tokens by 25% and disable non-essential features.

Example fallback YAML (route manifest snippet)

route: "text/generate/chat-v1"
primary_slice: "m-xlarge-fp32-v2"
fallbacks:
  - name: "m-xlarge-quant8-v2"
    reason: "FALLBACK_LATENCY"
  - name: "m-large-shortseq-quant8"
    reason: "DEGRADE_SHORT_SEQ"
degradation:
  - disable: ["streaming", "tool_calls"]
  - max_tokens_factor: 0.75

Observability contract

- Every routing event must emit: request_id, route, chosen_slice, reason_code, primary_p95_ms, current_error_rate_5m, node_id. These fields are indexed at ingest and available in the Console routing trace view.
- Create a derived SLI: fallback_rate_1h = count(requests with reason != PRIMARY)/count(total_requests) per route. Alert threshold = profile specific (default 1% for interactive, 5% for throughput).
- Unit of analysis window: 1m for latency, 5m for error_rate. Backing metrics must be stored for at least 30d.

SLOs & thresholds (recommended defaults)

- p50/p95/p99 latency goals by profile (from earlier table).
- Error rate (5m) alert if > 2% for interactive routes, > 5% for throughput routes.
- Fallback rate alert if > profile_alert_threshold for 15min sustained.

Operational playbook (high level)

1) Automated detection triggers fallback. Routing logs and traces visible in Console. If fallback_rate_1h > alert threshold, PagerDuty playbook starts.
2) Oncall actions (first 15 minutes):
   a) Verify whether fallback is due to load vs model regression. Check backend GPU utilization and node health pages.
   b) If load-related: increase capacity (scale pool) or temporarily increase fallback aggressiveness (move to next fallback).
   c) If regression-related: mark primary_slice unhealthy and route 100% to first fallback. Open a ticket with the Model Onboarding team; attach failing eval examples.
3) 15–60 minutes: rollback any recent model rollouts (if present), increase autoscaling min for affected pools, and notify Customer Success for high-visibility customers.
4) >60 minutes: escalate to L2 SRE and Model Reliability. Consider global throttles or traffic shaping per-customer.

Canary and rollout guidance (safety gates)

- A canary for a new slice must pass both a dry-run traffic profile (no routing change) and a soft canary (0.5% traffic) for 24 hours. Metrics to pass: fallback_rate within baseline +/- 0.2pp, p95 within baseline * 1.05, no increase in semantic-quality regression alerts.
- Rollouts are done with geometric traffic increases: 0.5%, 2%, 8%, 25%, 60% with 1–24 hour hold states based on route criticality.

Testing & evaluations required for slice compatibility

- Tokenization parity check (automated unit test).
- Deterministic prompt-responsiveness test (10k synthetic prompts).
- Latency distribution check under a standard replayed workload (10m at 2x baseline QPS).
- A minimum quality pass-rate on core eval set: 95% for interactive and 90% for throughput.

Example commands and debug checklist

- Check fallback rate for route:
  curl -sS "https://console.internal/api/v1/metrics?expr=fallback_rate_1h{route=\"text/generate/chat-v1\"}" | jq .
- Inspect routing trace for a failing request_id:
  rtr-cli trace --request request_id --fields route,chosen_slice,reason_code,node_id
- Force route to fallback locally for testing:
  rtr-cli route-set --route text/generate/chat-v1 --force-slice m-large-shortseq-quant8 --ttl 300

Ownership & responsibilities

- Route owners (service teams) must:
  - Declare the profile in route manifest.
  - Provide acceptable fallback slices and degradation knobs.
  - Maintain evaluation suites referenced by the route (links to eval harness).
- Serving Runtime team must:
  - Implement and maintain the routing engine and observability hooks.
  - Ship default profile templates.
  - Maintain runbooks and escalation paths.
- Model Onboarding team must:
  - Certify slice compatibility and maintain the slice catalog.

Decision record references

- This guideline implements policy from ADR: service-degradation-and-api-fallback-adr-2026 (see related_pages). It also depends on the observability SLI contract defined in observability-sli-tracing-and-cost-guardrails-adr-2024.

Appendix: Quick configuration table

Setting | Default | Notes
--------|---------|------
profile | interactive | set in route manifest
primary_slice | required | canonical model id
fallbacks | [] | ordered list; must be compatible
degradation_modes | [streaming,tool_calls] | optional list to toggle
fallback_thresholds.latency_multiplier | 1.25 | multiplier applied to profile p95
fallback_thresholds.error_rate_5m | 0.02 | proportion
auto_escalate | true | if true, triggers PagerDuty on sustained fallback

If you are a route owner and need help mapping an existing route to these profiles, open a ticket with tag: routing-help and include the route manifest.
